header: THE CHECK THAT READS THE CIRCULARS. Until 11 Nov 2026 I met every fault found in a briefing with one more rule in the prompt or one more regex (a wrong count, a discretion holder called an issuer, "directly" added, "Not stated" for an item the circular lists ...). Each such rule fixes the last question and nothing else. This module is the general form of all of them: after the best candidate is chosen, a SECOND model call reads the whole circular text and the briefing, and reports, sentence by sentence and cell by cell, what the circulars do not support, what they contradict, what the table lacks, which part of the question is unanswered, and what each short form stands for in these circulars. The verifier is itself a model, so I take nothing it says on trust. Plain code (applyVerdict) applies a report only when the code can check it:
- I use a corrected sentence or cell only when its figures are in the circulars (figuresSafe) and its wording is the circulars' wording;
- a quote the verifier gives must be found, verbatim, in the circular text, or I ignore the item;
- a sentence the circulars do not support, with no checkable correction given, is REMOVED: the briefing then says less, never more that is wrong;
- I never blank a cell on the verifier's word alone: "Not stated" is the absence check's business (absenceCheck.ts), which fills, never blanks.
Pure except for `verifyBriefing`, which makes the model call.

symbols.name: ambiguousShortForms
doc: Returns the short forms the briefing uses that have more than one confirmed sense (abbreviationSenses.ts), written as a short form (capitals, word on its own).

symbols.name: CODE_LIKE
doc: CLAUSES THE BRIEFING DOES NOT USE. A reader of a long circular misses a clause that bears on the question (a shorter limit for another case, a condition, an exception): the circular is long and the clause is one sentence. I let plain code narrow the haystack: the clauses (sentences) of the circulars that share at least two content words with the question and carry a figure the briefing never uses, the likeliest first. Code does not judge whether a clause belongs to the answer; it only points, and the verifier decides. I count as a code anything a reader acts on: letters with digits mixed (an IFSC code, a policy number) or a long run of digits (an account number); a telephone number is not one.

symbols.name: CLOCK
doc: TIMES UNDER THE WRONG NAME. A time is a fact only with its event ("Arrival and address of the Chief Guest 07:45", "Flag-off 08:00"): a briefing that puts the time under another name ("Assembly: 7:45 AM") misleads a reader who acts on it. Plain code compares: for each clock time of the briefing, I look for the words written just before it beside the same time in the circulars; when none of them stands there, the circulars' own words beside that time go to the verifier, who decides. Code only points.

symbols.name: MONTHS
doc: A LIST NAMED BUT NOT GIVEN. A circular holds a short list of dated entries (the five closed holidays: SAIL Foundation Day 24th January ...) under a heading whose words are the question's ("closed and public holidays"); the briefing says "5 closed holidays" or names them, and gives no date. A question that names the list asks for its entries. Plain code finds each short numbered list (3 to 20 entries) whose heading shares two words with the question and whose dated entries are, for the most part, dated nowhere in the briefing, and hands the entries over; the verifier decides and, when the list belongs to the answer, gives it under "unanswered" with the circular's own words.

symbols.name: verifierInput
symbols.sig: export function verifierInput(q: string, r: SynthesisResult, contextData: string): string
doc: Builds the user prompt of the verifier: the question, the briefing to check, the ambiguous short forms it must rule on, and the same circular records the writer saw.

symbols.name: titleCase
doc: Turns "STEEL AUTHORITY OF INDIA LIMITED" (a letterhead) into "Steel Authority of India Limited"; I leave a meaning that is not written in capitals as it is.

symbols.name: asList
doc: A value the verifier built from pieces of a list ("Republic Day ... May Day") reads as a list, so I turn the skipped-text marks into commas. (A quote keeps its marks: they are how it is checked.)

symbols.name: parseVerdict
symbols.sig: export function parseVerdict(raw: string): Verdict | null
doc: I read the verifier's JSON defensively: a field that is not of the expected shape becomes an empty list, never a crash. Returns null when there is no JSON at all.

symbols.name: flatText
doc: Keeps letters and digits only, one space between, thousands commas removed, so "Rs. 1,000/-" and "rs 1000" compare equal.

symbols.name: quotePieces
doc: The pieces of a quote. A quote may skip text with "..." ("SL. NO: 1 | HOLIDAY: Republic Day ... SL. NO: 4 | HOLIDAY: Mahatma Gandhi's Birthday"): then each piece is a quote of its own. I let a piece shorter than two words prove nothing, and a quote of more than eight pieces is not a quote.

symbols.name: quoteInSource
symbols.sig: export function quoteInSource(quote: string, flatSource: string): boolean
doc: True when the quote (every piece of it) is found verbatim, after flattening, in the source. I let a quote under 4 characters prove nothing.

symbols.name: wordingSupport
symbols.sig: function wordingSupport(text: string, srcStems: Set<string>): number
doc: Gives the share of the text's content words (stems) that the source also has: 1 when every word is the circular's.

symbols.name: alike
symbols.sig: function alike(a: string, b: string): number
doc: Scores how alike two sentences are, as the share of their words they have in common (1 = the same words).

symbols.name: findSentence
symbols.sig: function findSentence(sentences: string[], wanted: string): number
doc: Returns the index of the sentence of `text` that the verifier quoted (the same words, or nearly: a word the guards took out does not lose it), or -1.

members.name: sources
doc: Every circular the briefing was written from, with its text, because a quote names its circular.

members.name: figuresSafe
doc: Returns true when every figure in the text is in the circulars (the writer's own figure guard).

members.name: question
doc: The question asked. I want a part the verifier reports as unanswered to be made of the question's own words (optional: without it the check is not made).

members.name: changes
doc: One line per change made, for the log and the stored record.

members.name: ignored
doc: Counts the reports the code could not act on (a quote not found, a fix with a figure the circulars lack): I leave the briefing as it was there.

members.name: ignoredWhy
doc: One line per report left alone, saying which and why (for the log).

members.name: removed
doc: Counts the sentences removed as unsupported.

symbols.name: MAX_WITH_OMITTED
doc: A fact the circulars state and the briefing omits earns a place even when the writer used all six, so I allow two more, each one a checked sentence.

symbols.sig: export function applyVerdict(input: SynthesisResult, v: Verdict, ctx: RepairContext): RepairOutcome
doc: Applies what the verifier reported, to the extent plain code can check it. It never changes the input objects.
